newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain braces for more violence after Basque attack.
newsitem.headline: Spain braces for more violence after Basque attack.

text.p: A Spanish police inspector was gunned down on Thursday as security forces braced for a possible new wave of violence by Basque separatist rebels.

The killing, apparently carried out by the Basque guerrilla group ETA, came just hours after police went on nationwide alert and warned of possible attacks by the rebels, who have called for a "Day of Struggle" on Friday.
Police inspector Luis Andres Sanpedio was shot in the head outside his home in the northern Basque city of Bilbao by a lone gunman who fled by car.

ETA, which has often targeted members of the security forces in its 29-year campaign of violence for an independent Basque homeland, has been blamed for a series of 11 small bomb blasts in the past week.

Marking the two-year anniversary of a peace proposal the rebels themselves offered the government, ETA urged its followers on Friday to "fight and show our active opposition to the states that oppress us".
The rebels' 1995 offer was rejected by Spanish officials who have consistently refused to negotiate until ETA renounces violence.
ETA, which is fighting for an independent Basque region encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France, has killed some 800 people since 1968.
Observers in the Basque region say the past week's bomb attacks, which injured one person but mostly caused minor property damage, were part of a build-up to Friday.
"When they launch a challenge of this kind, they try all means to cause alarm..," Basque Interior Minister Jose Maria Atutxa told journalists.
"All of this could be backed by attacks of a bigger bloodier nature," he added.
Herri Batasuna, the political wing of ETA, and other groups linked to the violent campaign for independence have called for similar "action days" in solidarity with the rebels.
Spain's Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said his forces had taken the necessary steps to guarantee security and added that he hoped most Basques would ignore the rebel call for action.
"I'm confident in the response of the Basque society and in that every day ETA shows itself to be more and more outdated and out of place," he told journalists.
